title: Blob Storage from Applications
description: Upload, download, and manage blobs from C# and JavaScript applications using Azure SDKs.

data.text: Developers interact with Blob Storage through **Azure SDKs** or REST APIs. The SDKs handle authentication, retries, and serialization so you can focus on business logic. In this lesson, you will upload and download blobs, list container contents, and delete blobs from C# and JavaScript.

Applications can authenticate to storage using **connection strings**, **shared key signatures**, or **Azure AD** (via managed identity or service principals). For production, prefer Azure AD because it avoids long-lived secrets and integrates with role-based access control.

az storage blob upload-batch \
  --account-name stdemostorage \
  --destination uploads \
  --source ./exports \
  --auth-mode login

data.text: Every blob has system properties like content type, length, and last modified time. You can also set custom metadata. The SDK exposes these through the `Properties` and `Metadata` properties on the blob client.

data.title: Async All the Way
data.text: Azure SDK methods are async by default. Use await in your application code to keep threads free. Avoid .GetAwaiter().GetResult() in ASP.NET apps because it can cause deadlocks.

terms.definition: The top-level client for a storage account that provides access to containers.

A client scoped to a single blob, used to upload, download, and manage that blob.

data.title: Exercise: Build a Simple Uploader
data.description: Write a console app that uploads a file and lists all blobs in a container.
steps: Authenticate using DefaultAzureCredential or a connection string.
Upload a local file to a container.
List all blobs in the container and print their names and sizes.
data.expectedOutcome: A working console app that uploads and lists blobs in Azure Storage.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Azure SDKs provide typed clients for storage resources.
Use Azure AD authentication in production instead of connection strings.
BlobServiceClient -> BlobContainerClient -> BlobClient is the standard hierarchy.
Async methods keep your application responsive under load.
data.takeaway: You can now integrate Blob Storage directly into your applications using SDKs.
